design: MemorySearchService._require_unchanged(plan, candidate): _eligible on the exact ranked version plus stage-digest equality, else MemoryRetrievalError(REPRESENTATION_NOT_READY, CANDIDATE_CHANGED).

_materialize: per hit -- _require_unchanged, read_version, item digest check, stop epoch, _require_unchanged; after the loop and the receipt digest -- _require_unchanged for every ranked hit, then the stop epoch, then the audit write. The linearisation point of a successful search is the final sweep: a change committed after it is not reflected in that response (as for the stop epoch).

requirement_results.command: in every retrieval mode (STRUCTURED, FULL_TEXT, VECTOR, HYBRID) a REVOKED or QUARANTINED version (on the first and on the second hit read), a correction (new ACTIVE head) or a live materialisation-policy denial committed while the content of a ranked hit is being read fails the search closed with REPRESENTATION_NOT_READY/CANDIDATE_CHANGED: no hit, no success receipt, exactly one audited searchMemory.denied, and no further content read after the changed hit (RED on 0662051: the revoked/superseded/denied version was returned with a success receipt); after a correction the next search returns the new head and never v1 again

in every retrieval mode, the first materialised hit revoked while the second hit is read is caught by the re-validation of every hit right before the receipt, and a hit not yet read that is revoked while an earlier hit is read is refused by the pre-read check without its content ever being read: CANDIDATE_CHANGED, no hit, no success receipt, one audited denial (RED on 0662051 for the later-read case: both hits returned; the not-yet-read case passes on 0662051 too, guarding the pre-existing pre-read check)

positive counterparts on the same real backends: a revocation of an item outside the query (other kind) during the reads, and unchanged reads, return every hit with exactly one success receipt and no denial in every mode; a revocation after the response leaves the returned response unchanged and the next search excludes the revoked item; the worlds use the real version 2 PostgreSQL/Qdrant adapters and OpenBao transit

residual_risks: A change committed after the final sweep and before the response is returned is not reflected in that response; the receipt pins the exact versions served (same window as the stop epoch, REM-0020).
Each hit costs up to three eligibility evaluations (metadata reads and live materialisation-policy calls) instead of one; bounded by top_k.
F2 of REM-0020 (influence of policy-denied items) stays tracked toward FGM-16; unchanged by this remediation.
The PostgreSQL and Qdrant adapters remain the 0051 test adapters; no production adapter under memory/adapters/ exists yet.
Test-level anonymous Docker volume leaks of pre-existing suites remain allocated to OCOR-DEV-REM-0018 (full-suite resource attribution).

tdd.REFACTOR: The pre-read check and the two new checks share one helper (_require_unchanged). A first draft of the positive non-hit case used an EPISODIC item that is itself a candidate in STRUCTURED/VECTOR/HYBRID; it was corrected to an item of a kind outside the query. A first mutation probe on the first draft of the tests (raw label mutation-probe-first-result) left 3 of 6 mutants alive: (1) no post-read re-validation survived because the changed item was always the last one read, where the pre-receipt sweep also catches it -- the own-read case now changes the first and the second hit read and asserts that nothing is read after the changed hit; (2) no pre-read re-validation survived because no case changed a hit before its own read -- a case now revokes the hit not yet read while an earlier one is read and asserts its content is never read; (3) a mutant removing the lifecycle-status test inside the pre-existing 0052 _eligible is equivalent for every reachable state (every lifecycle transition commits a new head, so the unchanged head check already rejects the old version; non-ACTIVE first versions never reach the pool) and was replaced by a mutant of the new helper (accepting an ineligible version). The local commits were re-ordered before publication so that the final tests precede the fix (test-first), and the RED run was repeated on the final tests.
tdd.mutation_probe: 6 mutants of the remediation (no post-read re-validation, no pre-receipt sweep, sweep of the last hit only, no pre-read re-validation, the unchanged check accepting an ineligible version, a changed hit dropped silently instead of failing closed) run against the REM-0021, REM-0020 and 0052 suites on the real backends (raw label mutation-probe-result)
tdd.ordering_note: Test-first: the REM-0021 cases are the first commit of the change set and were run RED on the unremediated retrieval.py (tests-only commit) before the fix commit; the RED raw log prints the commit, its diff against origin/main and the byte identity of retrieval.py with origin/main.
